gaps: The libssh2 OpenSSL package candidate remains rejected by member hash, while the recipe-defined libssh2-wincng 1.11.1-2 package exactly matches the local DLL; this is package-member byte correspondence, not packaging approval.

The official installer archive members exactly match local tesseract.exe and libtesseract-5.dll. The official 5.5.3 source tag and UB build recipe are associated evidence; reproducible build equivalence is not asserted or required for this provenance observation.

The official installer GCC members exactly match local DLLs. Both approved Ubuntu Noble GCC runtime package candidates are hash/size-verified, but all four libgcc/libstdc++ comparisons have differing .text sections; this is code difference, not packaging metadata only. Their runtime data archives lack copyright text, so the matching base package is required for that evidence.
winpthreads has a matching candidate package member and an archived commit snapshot/COPYING, but the snapshot SHA-256 is observed only and not asserted upstream-proven.

All 39 bare recipe-declared downstream patches are archived with their declared recipe checksum verified. libarchive/backport-unzip.patch retains its historical raw-snapshot HTTP 404 alongside the exact recipe-declared remote commit-patch bytes that now verify.

BUILDINFO pkgbuild_sha256sum matches the archived pinned PKGBUILD for 19 of 27 original MSYS2 package candidates. Eight exact DLL-member packages have a differing BUILDINFO recipe hash, so their archived historical recipe/source/patch set remains a candidate rather than an exact build-recipe match.
Static PE closure was supplied as input; dynamic runtime loads and redistribution obligations were not determined by this audit.
